f46889ca5fb2454f8322.text: An informative text educates readers about a topic or subject. It is meant to

7f3900b01106fd11420e.text: inform others using credible sources as evidence – facts, statistics, and other research data. Informative texts usually answer the five Ws: who, where, when, what, and why. Sometimes, they also describe “how” to do or accomplish something.

45f4ea90bf3679852488.text: When choosing a topic for informative writing, focus on a specific topic.

a9d29ae58aa6d5aeb1f6.text: Consider the topic that is not too broad or too narrow. A topic is too broad if you cannot explain it in one or two pages. For example, you cannot choose special education as the topic because it has a big scope. Rather, you can be more specific and select causes of hearing-impairment as your topic. On the other hand, a topic is too narrow when it is very simple and can be explained in a sentence or a short paragraph.

4099ca826cf048c9d6cb.text: Just like any type of writing, informative texts follow a structure – the

0979b1fa1e385ff461d8.text: Grabbing the attention of readers is part of the beginning - formally known as

6cd3dbce9c422e77193c.text: introduction. It is where the thesis statement is found. The thesis statement is considered the most essential part of informative writing. According to Kristina Barroso in her article “Informative Writing Techniques”, the thesis statement is known as the road map of an informative text because the whole essay is built around it. The thesis sentence is a sentence that summarizes the entire essay.

f829cb5b12aa6173f497.text: Aside from stating the thesis statement, writers introduce the main

c5d323fb414c19b42380.text: idea, provide definition for difficult words/concepts, and give a short description on what will be discussed.

61b5fdd73228cc926c2f.text: The body or the middle part is where the thesis statement is fully explained.

aa2b04fc0c1b646f4d16.text: Evidence such as facts, statistics, statements from experts, and other supporting details are found in this section. This section requires citing sources of information. The evidence presented will be the basis if the information is reliable, accurate, and unbiased.

2c16f7fa0e385b03fd6a.text: The conclusion reiterates the thesis statement and summarizes the main

ad76ba0e062aadc0040c.text: points of the informative text. No new evidence must be presented at this point because all ideas must have already been discussed in the body.

6156aeb35b25715e52e1.text: Tone, clarity (being clear) and transition words

5d47c499c62638c3654b.text: Aside from the structure, other features and techniques of informative writing

9d2fb4159fe4339d735b.text: need to be considered. First is tone or attitude of the author toward the topic. The attitude of the author toward the topic should always be formal, objective, and neutral. As mentioned above, informative writing is fact-based - biased information is unacceptable. The writer’s opinion and beliefs do not have a place in informative writing. Second, always be specific. Provide clear answers to the five Ws and one H of the topic you are writing about. Employ language that is clear, formal, and unbiased. Also, do not forget to use transitional words (discussed in previous modules) for organized and smooth flow of ideas. In doing so, readers can get a better understanding of the information they read.

53f004e316a6f6cd0663.text: Informative essays vary in length, but all good informative pieces are a product

be17006aa935d560d20e.text: of an application of several writing techniques. Below are some of the best tips/techniques to help you write an excellent informative text. 1. Open with an attention grabber and conclude with a summary of the main

93188b8650e348f061e5.text: points of the essay. 2. Use appropriate transitional words to ensure the logical flow of ideas. 3. Observe formal tone. 4. Utilize proper language and applicable vocabulary to the topic. Similarly, avoid biased language. 5. Make use of formatting, nonlinear texts such as flowcharts, graphs, graphic organizers, and digital texts with hyperlinks when needed.

2a10b4a76d7502b1c148.text: Now, check out this example of an informative essay, and try to analyze if the aforementioned techniques were used in this writing.

626a04f4ff8c379bbd6a.text: The new normal has limited face-to-face interactions, which is why

132687b0a73ad1fae880.text: people shifted to sending emails and chats to transact business. This also has become the set-up even in the educational setting; teachers, learners, and parents communicate with one another through chat or email.

422decbe448692be6e60.text: However, while this medium is more efficient, this could disrupt the

abdd5ea1972c0acc4f12.text: communication process especially if the message is not clearly and coherently. The learner may not be aware that emails and chats are also formal correspondence and ends up sending friendly and informal messages to his teachers. The result? Seen-zoned messages, without reply. To avoid miscommunication, follow these email tips, rules, and examples outlined by educator Katie Azevedo.

46ca241c7eb789796f0f.text: First, enter a subject line (for email). This tells the receiver if the

19a44efee0f0465700fb.text: message is important, urgent, work-related and whatnot. Secondly, use a proper greeting or salutation just like you do in business letters. Next, introduce yourself by stating your name and your class or section. This is necessary since teachers have hundreds of students to attend to.

037b3a74149bc33d7059.text: After these preliminaries state your concern, preferably by starting

7cce6d8be8598af990a2.text: with an overview sentence. Keep it short and simple, and remind yourself to use appropriate language; jokes, sarcasm, and emojis are not necessary.

58452ce3b91baf6c8457.text: Lastly, thank your teacher and close out the email or chat. Remember

ce12b8558534d9ca2839.text: not to demand an immediate reply.

1e944e82f8ff8b49198a.text: These tips and rules send a message that you only mean business;

291d3ceced6004be5e8e.text: hence you are likely to get the answers you are seeking. This is not just a school-skill; this will be applicable even when you will be applying for a job or when you are emailing or sending chats to your boss.

d6459a13c1391c691ad0.text: Emails and chats are indeed an effective and efficient forms of

af1b8558ad8993c9e2b4.text: communication, especially if done correctly, simply, and respectfully.

d3c1d717b9287be60b07.text: This essay is probably way shorter than most informative essays, but does it

3a65e4437af1d4b6cbce.text: comply to the prescribed structure and conventions in informative writing? Does it comply to the guidelines and techniques?

8be6fa80b286b4c3b81c.text:  It started with a relatable scenario and ended with a repeat of the thesis statement.  It utilized transitional words such as ‘however, first, second, next, after, lastly.’  The tone is generally formal, but it becomes conversational in parts where the essay shifts to a second person point of view.  The language used is simple and appropriate for the target audience – students.  There aren’t any graphics or visuals, but they are not really necessary considering the length of the essay and the topic. However, in online platforms, this essay could be presented in a bullet list with and with other nonlinear texts.

7488ce2bed92aa6b8880.text: Informative writing plays a vital role not only in the academic world but also

6c7da9bc42c693029829.text: in the real world. It is a skill so essential that it can affect your grades and future job opportunities. Becoming an effective writer is not easy, but it pays to be one.

reference-clarification.text: Informative writing explains a topic with balanced factual information. Persuasive writing aims to gain agreement with a viewpoint, supporting that viewpoint with facts.
